<!-- Generated by codeflower-app's cmd/gendocs: do not edit. -->

Rerun a reproducible pipeline archive, which an agent made with codeflower-repro in a sandbox, and compare its results with those it recorded. ARCHIVE is the NAME.tar.gz file, its URL, or an unpacked pipeline folder.

No agent is involved and no sign-in is needed. In a new sandbox with a new, throwaway project, it:

```sh
1. downloads the archive's input data and checks each file's sha256 (on this
   computer, into a temporary folder, or kept in --cache), and checks the
   archive (no network);
2. restores the software environment from the archive's lockfiles: only the
   package indexes (PyPI, conda, CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub) are reachable
   where the engine can restrict the network (Linux, Apptainer); on macOS and
   Windows the network is not restricted, which the summary says. With
   --snapshot, the environment packed beside the archive is unpacked instead,
   without network;
3. runs the pipeline without network, and compares every result with the
   recorded one, exactly or within the tolerance its two runs showed.
```

The output folder gets results/, logs/ (one per rule), the run's time and memory (run.json), the comparison (reproduce-report.md and .json) and everything the sandbox printed (reproduce.log; --verbose also shows it here). Nothing else stays on this computer: the unpacked archive, the downloads (unless --cache) and the throwaway project are removed when the run ends, also after a failure or Ctrl-C. A run that was killed leaves them in the temporary folder, and the next run removes them and its containers.

The image is the archive's: pulled by its digest when it was published, or the local build it names. --image runs another one, which can change results.

Exit status: 0 reproduced, 1 results differ, 2 the archive is not valid, 3 no container engine, 4 the environment could not be restored, 5 the pipeline failed, 130 stopped (Ctrl-C).


## Usage

```sh
codeflower reproduce ARCHIVE --output DIR [flags]
```

## Examples

```sh
  codeflower reproduce smith2026.tar.gz --output ~/repro/smith2026
  codeflower reproduce https://zenodo.org/records/123/files/smith2026.tar.gz -o repro
  codeflower reproduce smith2026.tar.gz --snapshot smith2026-env-amd64.tar.gz -o repro
  codeflower reproduce smith2026.tar.gz --validate -o check
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cache string` |  | folder to keep downloaded archives and data in for later runs (default: a temporary folder, removed afterwards) |
| `--cores int` |  | cores the pipeline may use (default: the archive's) |
| `--cpus int` |  | CPUs the sandbox may use (Docker and Podman) |
| `--engine string` | `auto` | container engine: auto, docker, podman, or apptainer (or set $CODEFLOWER_ENGINE) |
| `--image string` |  | run this image instead of the archive's (a Docker/Podman image name, or an Apptainer .sif file) |
| `--keep-state` |  | keep the run's temporary folder (the throwaway project, the unpacked archive), to look into a failure |
| `--memory string` |  | memory the sandbox may use, e.g. 16g (Docker and Podman) |
| `-o, --output string` |  | folder for the results, logs and report (created) |
| `--snapshot string` |  | restore the environment from this snapshot (NAME-env-ARCH.tar.gz, packed with the archive) instead of the lockfiles |
| `--validate` |  | only check the archive and its data; do not run it |
| `-v, --verbose` |  | show the sandbox's output (Snakemake, the package installs) here, not only in reproduce.log |
